3500_2019.selection_event: p5, p23, p29: 'On 1 January 2019, Syndicate 3500 accepted the reinsurance to close of the liabilities of another Lloyd's syndicate, a runoff syndicate with underwriting years of 2016 and prior ... gross and net technical provisions of approximately 560 million and 419 million'. p23: 'These liabilities are shown in the below triangles in their original underwriting years.' Effective 1 Jan 2019 = opening of year t, so it sits BETWEEN no diagonals: it is inside the end-2018 diagonal as printed in the 2019 table (as if always) but was not in 3500's own end-2018 balance sheet. Functional currency changed USD to GBP the same day (p6, p19).
3500_2019.acquired_syndicate: Syndicate 3210 (MS Amlin / MSI Corporate Capital). Not named on any 3500 page. Named in 3210's own 2018 report: p6 'The syndicate has closed into Riverstone syndicate 3500 with effect from 1 January 2019'; p16 'has reinsured to close its 2016 and prior years of account into Riverstone syndicate 3500 from 1 January 2019'; p43 post balance sheet event. 3210 p41 gross reserve 559,412 = 3500's 'approximately 560 million'; 3210 net 417,228 vs 3500 'approximately 419 million' (1.8m apart). Other 2018-19 transactions (Syndicate 2987 Brit LPT 30 Nov 2018; a third-party syndicate LPT 21 Dec 2018) sit in the 2018 column only (3500 2019 p23, p29; 3500 2018 p36) and do not touch u<=2017 rows.

end2018_diagonal_tie.source: syndicate_3210_2018 p41 'Claims development ... gross ... Balances have been translated at exchange rates prevailing at 31 December 2018' (GBP 000), columns 2011-2016 plus '2010 and prior' reserve 62,788; total gross reserve 559,412
end2018_diagonal_tie.result: Every one of the 33 gross cells of 3210's 2011-2016 triangle (all development ages, not only the diagonal) equals the 3500 2019 table cell divided by a single factor 0.96142-0.96143 (ratio range 0.961422 to 0.961429 across all 33 cells; differences are rounding). Same factor for 3500's OWN 2018 column: 2018 first-year cell 192,223 vs 199,935 printed in 3500's 2018 report p23 (ratio 0.961427). Net triangle shows the same factor (e.g. 2011 first cell 63,443 vs 3210 net 65,989). So the whole 2019 table is the sum of 3500's own 2018 report (only a 2009 column and the 2018 column, 3500 has NO own 2011-2016 cells) and 3210's own 2018 triangle, all restated at one uniform factor (consistent with the whole table being moved to end-2019 sterling rates; the pages print no rates, so the cause is an inference). Because the factor is uniform across both diagonals and every cohort, it does not distort M: M at 3210's own end-2018 rates would be 27.5m vs 26.4m declared.
end2018_diagonal_tie.paid_bridge: 3210 p41 cumulative paid (118958, 125644, 148078, 174337, 211618, 144875) times 0.96143, against 3500 2019 p24 cumulative paid (117392, 126449, 150104, 214548, 241721, 194618) gives 2019 payments by cohort 3026, 5655, 7742, 46940, 38271, 55335 = 156,969; plus 2018 column 40,096 (or 40,906, see note) = about 197.1m; gross claims paid 2019 = 204,711 (p13, note 7 p30), so prior-years payments are the residual 7.6m (3.7%), plausible.

3500_2019.overlap: The u<=2017 rows carry the acquired syndicate's history (3210's 2011-2016 years of account), restated 'as if always' in original years. That is the original-cohort history, not another vehicle's duplicate: 3500 had no own 2011-2016 cells in 2018 (p23 of the 2018 report shows only 2009 and 2018 columns, prior years 59,855), so nothing is counted twice and no cohort is reassigned or merged.
3500_2019.gross_net: Gross and net triangles both printed (p24); both carry the same 0.96143 factor against 3210's gross and net triangles. Gross cells are gross (est less paid = printed liability for every cohort). No net RITC premium enters a gross row (RITC booked gross 552,752, ceded 122,657, p30).
3500_2019.closing_tie: End-2019: est less paid by cohort = printed liability (11,295; 17,086; 34,056; 61,738; 91,128; 131,662; 149,665) sum 496,630; plus prior years 90,341 = 586,971 = balance sheet claims outstanding (p15) = note 7 closing (p30). Table total est 1,582,368 = sum of columns.

incurred_test.calc: sum over columns of latest less previous diagonal: 3224 + 2108 - 4810 + 1988 + 14748 + 9186 + (2018 col 190571 - 192223 = -1652) = 24,792; there is no 2019 column
incurred_test.accounts: P&L p13: gross claims paid 204,711 + change in gross provision 352,787 = gross claims incurred 557,498 (segmental p29: (557,498)); this includes the RITC booked as premium 430,858 and claims 552,752 (note 7 'Reinsurance of new liabilities 552,752'). Excluding the RITC: 557,498 - 552,752 = 4,746.
incurred_test.comparison: The table omits the prior-years reserve, so 24.8m alone cannot be compared with 557.5m or 4.7m. Adding the prior years: opening prior-year reserve = 3500's own 59,855 (2018 report p23) plus 3210's 62,788 (p41) all at the 0.96143 factor = 117,913 (or 120,221 if 3500's own is left unscaled); closing 90,341; prior-years paid 7,646 (residual above): prior-year incurred about -19.9m (or -22.2m). Table total 24.8 - 19.9 = +4.9m (or +2.6m) against 4.7m ex-RITC in the accounts: ties within 0.2m (or 2.2m). This is my derivation; the prior-years column is not printed as a triangle. FX is not separable on the pages: the note 7 'Change in estimates ... including foreign exchange' is -20,860, and the P&L change in provision differs from the balance-sheet movement (352,787 vs 327,181) by 25,606, unexplained on the pages.
incurred_test.control_2018: not a like-for-like control: the 2018 report's gross table has only the 2009 and 2018 columns (p23) and 2018 incurred is dominated by the two LPTs (199,935).

3500_2019.printed_slip: 3500 2019 p24, 2018 column, gross 'Cumulative payments to date' prints 40,096 but 190,571 - 149,665 (printed liability) = 40,906 and the printed total paid 1,085,738 needs 40,906. A transposition in a u=2018 cell, outside M; no effect on u<=2017.
3500_2019.unreconciled_small: The roll-forward RITC line 552,752 (p30) is 6.7m (1.2%) below 3210's printed gross reserve 559,412 and 14.9m (2.8%) above that reserve at the 0.96143 factor; the cohort cells do not depend on it.
3500_2019.M_reconstructed_or_validated: VALIDATED at both ends. End-2019 cells tie to paid plus liability by cohort and to the balance sheet; end-2018 cells tie cell by cell, at one factor, to the acquired syndicate's own 2018 filing and (for 2018) to 3500's own 2018 report. M follows from the acquired syndicate's own history plus its 2019 development, with no FX difference between diagonals.
3500_2019.reason: The concern was real (an acquired run-off book restated 'as if always' into 2011-2016 columns on the day the functional currency changed), but the acquired syndicate is 3210 and its own 2018 triangle reproduces every end-2018 cell of the 2019 table at one uniform factor, so the end-2018 diagonal is validated and M (+26.4m) is the original-cohort outcome at one rate.

3000_2016.closing_tie: Table est less paid by cohort at end-2016 = printed provision for every column (81,007; 126,621; 109,756; 167,014; 175,085; 119,564) and with all-prior-years 324,217 sums to 1,103,264 (printed total; note 18 p37: 737,922 + 248,822 - 19,130 + 135,650 = 1,103,264). Reader 2's tie is correct.

overlap_and_fx.finding_1: The 2016 table's 2011-2013 history is NOT the sum of the two printed 2015 tables: +454m (49%) at end-2015 in estimate and +449m in paid. First-year cells tie within 1.4-2.1% (FX-sized); the excess builds in later development years (e.g. 2011 incremental paid in the 'two years later' step: 142.7m in the 2016 table vs 81.8m in the sum of the printed tables). The pages give no explanation of the excess. (My observation only: the paid excess net of a 1.2147 revaluation is about 333m, close to the RITC 248,822 plus 1400's all-prior-years provision 85,422 = 334.2m; not established.)
overlap_and_fx.finding_2_mixed_rates: The end-2015 diagonal is not at one rate. For the 3000-only cohorts 2014 and 2015 the end-2015 paid cell is the printed 2015 paid times 1.2147 and 1.2069 (69,541 vs 57,251; 11,644 vs 9,648), i.e. revalued to 2016 rates, but the end-2015 estimate cell is only 1.0517 and 1.0182 times the printed estimate, because it equals revalued paid plus the unrevalued 2015 balance-sheet reserve (230,985 = 69,541 + 161,444; 103,960 = 11,644 + 92,316). The end-2016 diagonal is wholly at 2016 rates. So M includes the retranslation of the opening mature-cohort reserves (544,540 at end-2015 rates, u<=2014).
overlap_and_fx.fx_size_estimate: Note 18 p37 'Movement due to foreign exchange 135,650' is 13.75% of opening plus RITC (986,744). Applied to the 544,540 of mature-cohort opening reserves: about +74.9m inside M, which would leave about -47.5m at one rate (about -89.6m if the 1.2147 paid revaluation applied to all of it). These are my order-of-magnitude derivations, not printed figures; but any version is 2.7 times M or more, and the sign flips. Management states a favourable prior-year movement: 'Net reserves for claims outstanding at 31 December 2015 were reduced by 57.6m in calendar year 2016' (p33), against M = +27.3m (adverse).

3000_2016.gross_net: Gross table is gross; net table (p38) separate; RITC net 223,669 shown only in the note. No gross/net mixing found in the gross rows.

incurred_test.calc: 3117 - 1558 - 27690 + 53456 + (2015: 252441 - 103960 = 148481) + (2016 first cell 142,410) = 318,216 (reader 1's +318m confirmed; it omits the 'all prior years' column and FX)
incurred_test.accounts_without_RITC: P&L p16: gross claims paid (264,295), change in gross provision +19,130 => gross claims incurred 245,165 (reader 1's 245m confirmed). The RITC 248,822 is not in the P&L claims lines; it is a separate line in the note 18 roll-forward (p37).
incurred_test.like_for_like: Table-implied TOTAL gross movement including all-prior-years = closing 1,103,264 - opening 973,476 (= 737,922 3000 + 235,554 1400, the two printed 2015 balance-sheet provisions) + paid 264,295 = 394,083. Accounts: incurred 245,165 + FX 135,650 + (RITC 248,822 - 1400's own closing provision 235,554 = 13,268) = 394,083. Closes to the unit with the RITC OUTSIDE incurred. So the 30% gap in reader 1's comparison is the omitted prior-years column and FX, not by itself evidence of overlapping history; with the RITC added to incurred the test would not close (493,987).
incurred_test.paid_test: Table implied 2016 paid, printed columns 176,026 (7,803 + 15,509 + 16,270 + 47,886 + 65,712 + 22,846); accounts 264,295; implied prior-years paid 88,269.

3000_2016.M_reconstructed_or_validated: Reconstructed arithmetically as a reported-currency movement: M = 2016 payments on the 2011-2014 cohorts 87,468 (7,803+15,509+16,270+47,886) + change in their reserves (end-2016 484,398 less end-2015 544,540 = -60,142) = 27,325, with both reserve ends tied to balance-sheet provisions (end-2015 to the two printed 2015 reports to the unit). NOT validated as an original-cohort outcome: (a) the end-2015 diagonal is a mixed-rate cell (see finding_2), so M carries about 75m of retranslation that cannot be split by cohort from the pages; (b) 449m-454m of unexplained extra cumulative history in 2011-2013; (c) the payments by cohort are validated only in total (prior-years paid is a residual).
3000_2016.reason: The closing diagonal ties and the RITC is outside incurred, so the other reading is right on those two points, but the end-2015 cells are revalued paid plus an unrevalued reserve, so M (+27.3m) includes the retranslation of the opening reserves (about 75m on the note's own FX rate, which would turn M negative and agrees with the stated 57.6m favourable release), and the 2011-2013 history sits 454m (49%) above the two printed 2015 tables with no explanation; no defensible constant-currency original-cohort figure can be built from the pages. If the paper's M is defined as the printed reported-currency table movement, the arithmetic reconstruction above would instead make this concern_resolved.
